about:
The docs sections in menu order (PLAN.md File tree; ids from docs/research/02 §1, and the sections Phase 4 adds from docs/research/04 §1). build.mjs assembles them into the one docs page, docs.html, and generates its side nav from this file: each category is a
in the nav, and each section a link to # (build.mjs header comment, step 3). Per section: id, the section's id, which its file site/docs/sections/.html puts on its hgroup's h1; title, that h1's text; description, the sentence of its hgroup's

as plain text; and label, its nav link as HTML, only where that is not the title. The migration section has no title or description here: both hold the name criterion 14 allows only in that section's own file, so its nav link takes the content of the file's h1 (build.mjs, step 3).

sections.title: Quick start
sections.description: Link femto from a CDN, a download or npm, and plain HTML looks clean and readable.

sections.title: Theme picker
sections.description: Choose a theme color and options, and copy the links that load them.

sections.title: Themes
sections.description: femto's built-in color is azure, and each of the 19 others is one file in css/themes/.

sections.title: Options
sections.description: Each file in css/options/ changes one default.

sections.title: Color schemes
sections.description: femto has a light and a dark color scheme, which follow the visitor's system setting unless you choose one with data-theme.

sections.title: Colors
sections.description: femto.colors.css holds the palette of femto's 20 theme colors, in 19 shades each, as custom properties and utility classes.

sections.title: CSS variables
sections.description: Change femto's fonts, spacing, borders and colors by setting its --femto-* custom properties in your own CSS.

sections.title: Container
sections.description: Use .container to center the content at a maximum width for each breakpoint, or .container-fluid to span the full width.

sections.title: Landmarks and sections
sections.description: The page's header, main and footer, and every section, get vertical spacing.

sections.title: Nav
sections.description: <nav> lays out its lists in one row, with their links, buttons and form fields lined up.

sections.title: Grid
sections.description: .grid lays its children out in equal columns from 768px, and in one column below.

sections.title: Card
sections.description: An <article> is a card: a padded block with rounded corners, a background and a shadow.

sections.title: Overflow auto
sections.description: .overflow-auto scrolls content that overflows it, such as a wide table.

sections.title: Typography
sections.description: The root font size steps up at each breakpoint, and text elements are sized relative to it, so text grows with the screen.

sections.title: Link
sections.description: Links use the primary color, and .secondary or .contrast gives them the secondary or contrast color.

sections.title: Button
sections.description: A plain <button> needs no class and has the primary color by default.

sections.title: Table
sections.description: A <table> fills the width of its container, with padded cells, a line under each row and a line above the footer.

sections.title: Forms overview
sections.label: Overview
sections.description: Form fields are styled from their elements alone, and text inputs, selects and textareas fill the width of their container.

sections.title: Input
sections.description: Text, date, search and color inputs share one field style; file inputs, checkboxes, radios, switches and range have their own look.

sections.title: Textarea
sections.description: <textarea> has the style of the other fields, and the visitor can resize it vertically.

sections.title: Select
sections.description: <select> has the style of the other fields, with a chevron at the end.

sections.title: Checkboxes
sections.description: <input type="checkbox"> is drawn as a bordered box that fills with the primary color and a check when checked.

sections.title: Radios
sections.description: <input type="radio"> is drawn as a circle with a thick ring in the primary color when checked.

sections.title: Switch
sections.description: <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> is a switch: a checkbox drawn as a sliding toggle.

sections.title: Range
sections.description: <input type="range"> is a full-width slider with a thin track and a round thumb.

sections.title: Accordion
sections.description: A <details> is an accordion: its <summary> opens and closes the content, without JavaScript.

sections.title: Dropdown
sections.description: <details class="dropdown"> is a dropdown: a <summary> and a <ul> that opens below it.

sections.title: Group
sections.description: role="group" joins buttons, inputs and selects in one row, and role="search" also rounds its ends.

sections.title: Loading
sections.description: aria-busy="true" shows a loading spinner before an element’s content.

sections.title: Modal
sections.description: A <dialog> holding an <article> is a modal: a card centered over the page.

sections.title: Progress
sections.description: <progress> is a full-width rounded bar in the primary color.

sections.title: Tooltip
sections.description: data-tooltip shows its text in a tooltip on hover and focus, without JavaScript.

sections.title: Files
sections.description: femto comes in two forms that style a page the same way: one file in dist/, or the modules it is built from in css/.

sections.title: Custom module set
sections.description: To load only some modules, save a copy of css/femto.css in the same folder and delete the lines you do not need.

sections.title: Cascade layer
sections.description: femto is not in a cascade layer: to put it in one, import it with layer(), with your theme and option files in the same layer.

sections.title: Shadow roots
sections.description: femto declares its tokens on :host as well as :root, so it also styles the inside of a shadow root that loads it.

sections.title: Classes and attributes
sections.description: Most of femto works from the elements alone; these are the classes and attributes it also reads.

sections.title: RTL
sections.description: Set dir="rtl" for right-to-left text, and femto mirrors the parts of its components that have a direction.

sections.title: Browser support
sections.description: femto targets Baseline Widely Available on its release date: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 128, Safari 17.5 and Samsung Internet 27.
